english.title: Fail to comply with a serious crime prevention order
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without reasonable excuse, failed to comply with a serious crime prevention order made under section 1 of the Serious Crime Act 2007 by **(..SPECIFY THE COURT AND LOCATION..) on **(..SPECIFY THE DATE..) in that **(..SPECIFY THE FAILURE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 25 of the Serious Crime Act 2007.

english.notes:
(i) Section 25(4) of the Serious Crime Act 2007 provides that in proceedings for an offence under this section, a copy of the original order or any variation of it, certified as such by the proper officer of the court which made it, is admissible as evidence of its having been made and of its contents to the same extent that oral evidence of those things is admissible in those proceedings.
(ii) A Serious Crime Prevention Order can be made against a body corporate as a limited liability partnership (section 30), any other partnership (section 31) or an unincorporated association (section 32).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022, see section 25(2) of, and paragraph 4 of Schedule 13 to, the Serious Crime Act 2007; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 25(2) and (3A) of that Act and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
